items.title: Exporters may be asked to monitor supply chains' indirect emissions
items.summary: The Indian government is engaging in discussions about measuring Scope 3 emissions for exporters. This consideration arises as trade partners impose tighter green requirements globally. Current frameworks focus on direct emissions and exclude indirect ones, making compliance more complex. As a result, industries, especially MSMEs, may face compliance burdens if new requirements are implemented. Ultimately, the aim is to ensure that Indian exporters remain competitive in international markets.

Feed manufacturers are also feeling the impact as higher prices reduce demand for their products.

items.title: Global investors against use of judicial anti-avoidance rule by tax officials

items.title: India's exports rise across geographies; Africa, ASEAN lead growth in Apr-Aug

Exports to Africa saw a notable rise of 47 percent, reaching USD 26.19 billion. The ASEAN region also experienced a substantial growth of 56 percent in exports, totaling USD 23.08 billion. Furthermore, shipments to North-East Asia rose by 37 percent, amounting to USD 21.03 billion. Overall, India's total merchandise exports rose by 18.

items.title: Faster services imports threaten to erode cushion against India’s goods trade deficit: Report
items.summary: India's services trade surplus has declined as imports grew faster than exports, leading to concerns about foreign exchange earnings. In September 2026, net services exports fell by 10 percent to USD 16.9 billion. Despite strong growth in merchandise exports of 23 percent, the services sector faces challenges. While cumulative net services exports increased during the first half, their sustainability is uncertain.
